source.title: Understanding AdamW through Proximal Methods and Scale-Freeness
source.authors: Zhenxun Zhuang; Mingrui Liu; Ashok Cutkosky; F. Orabona

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Compares AdamW with Adam-ℓ2 on image classification and measures test performance and update-scale distributions, bearing on the adaptive-optimizer and decoupled-weight-decay part of V4 using a different comparison from the version's Adam-versus-SGD evidence.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons and update-scale measurements. Hyperparameter grid ranges and values used to select settings are setup, not result rows. SGD divergence is stated for one setting and is included as a row. No random-label or memorization-capacity experiment is reported.
record.test_reason: The study tests V4's decoupled-weight-decay component in CIFAR image classifiers with and without Batch Normalization. Its own held-out results compare tuned AdamW with tuned Adam-ℓ2. They do not establish whether either closes a performance gap relative to SGD.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately describes the main empirical conclusion: AdamW improves training and test performance over Adam-ℓ2 in very deep networks without BN, and this advantage correlates with concentrated update scales rather than establishing causality. A fuller account should also include the theoretical and empirical connection between AdamW and proximal updates.
record.recipe_differences: Compares AdamW with Adam-ℓ2, not the Adam-versus-SGD comparisons central to V4; both methods were tuned over learning rate and weight decay. The paper studies CIFAR image classifiers, Batch Normalization settings, and update-scale distributions.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch Normalization changes the observed AdamW advantage; network depth is reported to make the advantage more evident; multiplying the loss by 10 or 100 changes Adam-ℓ2 behavior substantially while AdamW remains approximately scale-free.

fits_no_version.finding: AdamW's update magnitudes are more concentrated than Adam-ℓ2's without BN, with greater differences at greater depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Update-scale concentration correlates with AdamW's training and test-performance advantage in deep image classifiers without BN.

fits_no_version.finding: Multiplying the loss by 10 or 100 approximately preserves AdamW's performance surface and optimal hyperparameters, while substantially changing Adam-ℓ2's.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: AdamW remains approximately scale-free with the small nonzero epsilon used in these experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Momentum SGD with weight decay 0.0001 diverges on a 110-layer ResNet without BN even at learning rate 1e-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Momentum SGD can encounter severe training instability in this deep network when BN is removed.

record.problems: The central generalization comparisons are presented in figures without numerical values in the supplied text. The authors report no uncertainty estimates. The link between update-scale concentration and performance is explicitly correlational, and the paper says it does not rule out other possible causes.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result rows were omitted. Figure 2 and Figure 3 exact plotted values were not reconstructed from figures; their rows retain figure-only values and use the accompanying text for state.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.

Adaptive-versus-SGD held-out rankings; recovery of an SGD-relative gap through decoupled weight decay; matched training-performance comparisons; broader optimizer tuning; switching to SGD; language benchmarks. The study tunes learning rate and weight decay, fixes Adam's other parameters, and directly tests only AdamW versus Adam-ℓ2.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects, small-data regimes, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples versus equally sized random removals and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. Verdicts concern its decoupled-weight-decay component only. Exact plotted errors and uncertainty estimates are unavailable in the supplied text. Best settings were selected using test error, and each configuration used one fixed initialization across optimizers and hyperparameters. Figures 5–6 compare proximal optimizer variants and do not provide additional tests of the listed versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image generalization.

The study does not compare Adam or AdamW against SGD or momentum SGD across the image and language benchmarks in the version, nor test broader tuning, switching optimizers, or word-level language models. It compares AdamW with Adam-ℓ2.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout and weight-decay removal with or without augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing influential memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: 110 Layer Resnet on CIFAR10
rows.operation_detail: Compared AdamW and Adam-ℓ2 training curves at each optimizer's settings with smallest test error.
rows.measure: Training loss and test accuracy over training
rows.note: Authors state AdamW both improves test accuracy and trains much faster; the curves are not numerically transcribed.
rows.check: Split training loss and test accuracy into separate measures. Only the test-accuracy component directly bears on V4; it overlaps R8 and is not independent evidence. Faster training does not establish better generalization at matched training performance.

rows.subject: 110 Layer Resnet on CIFAR10

rows.note: The figure is described as showing near-invariance for AdamW and drastic changes for Adam-ℓ2, but this row's test-error measure does not directly report the V4 comparison against SGD.
rows.check: The stated result concerns invariance to loss scaling, not a reported AdamW-versus-Adam-ℓ2 performance ranking or an adaptive-versus-SGD generalization comparison.

rows.subject: 110 Layer Resnet on CIFAR10

rows.baseline: Adam-ℓ2 update scales are more dispersed
rows.value: AdamW update scales are more concentrated
rows.note: The study reports this as an empirical correlate of AdamW's advantage. It is not the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7.
rows.check: Update-coordinate concentration is observed, but it measures neither held-out performance nor V7's tolerance to magnitude-scaled weight perturbations.

rows.subject: 110 Layer Resnet on CIFAR10

rows.measure: Distribution of absolute update-coordinate magnitudes divided by α
rows.baseline: Adam-ℓ2 updates become more dispersed with depth
rows.value: AdamW updates remain in a more concentrated scale range
rows.note: Appendix describes histograms for each ResNet depth; the text states the depth trend, not numerical distribution summaries.
rows.check: The subject is incorrectly restricted to the 110-layer model: Figures 7–11 cover ResNets with 20, 44, 56, 110 and 218 layers. Split by depth. Update concentration cannot determine any listed version's effect.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 ResNets and CIFAR-100 DenseNet-BC without Batch Normalization, with learning rate and weight decay tuned for both optimizers
relationships.reason: R5–R10 report better held-out performance for AdamW than Adam-ℓ2, especially in deeper networks, supporting the benefit of decoupled weight decay without demonstrating recovery relative to SGD.
relationships.display_finding: AdamW performed better than Adam with L2 regularization, especially in deeper networks, without establishing recovery relative to SGD.
